bindings.label: Infant presented with nystagmus and right exotropia
No family history of retinoblastoma; known untreated atrial septal defect
Fundus examination revealed bilateral involvement, with a tumor in the right eye and an isolated anterior tumor in the left eye

Neurological examination initially normal at baseline; two days after procedure, patient presented with status epilepticus and left upper extremity weakness; follow-up at 6 months showed full strength in the upper and lower extremities and normal tone
Echocardiography confirmed a moderate left-to-right shunt without thrombus or vegetation
Brain MRI shows right MCA territory infarct with absent A1 segment
RB1 germline testing and orbital MRI remain unavailable, so heritable risk and extraocular extension cannot be fully excluded
